topics.name: Degrees of comparison (the more ... the more)
Relative pronouns who, which, whose, that

options: The lion drank some water from the river.
The lion drank some waters from the river.
The lion drank a water from the river.
questions.rule: Water is uncountable: no a and no plural -s. Say some water.

options: The vulture flew over two country.
The vulture flew over two countries.
The vulture flew over a countries.
questions.rule: Two needs a plural noun. Country becomes countries (y after a consonant → ies).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: golden
gold
goldsmith

questions.rule: Gold is an uncountable noun, so it has no plural: a lot of gold.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: watches
watched
watching

questions.rule: These ... are needs a plural noun. Words ending in -ch add -es: watches.

options: many
a few
much
questions.rule: Use much with uncountable nouns like water; many and a few go with countable nouns.

options: tallest
more tall
taller
questions.rule: Comparing two with than needs the comparative: short adjective + -er = taller.
We count milk with a unit: a glass of milk, never a milk.

chat: How many eggs do we need for the cake?
options: We need three egg.
We needs three eggs.
We need three eggs.
questions.rule: Three takes a plural noun: eggs. With we, the verb is need.

chat: What did you see at the zoo?
options: I saw two lions and three foxes.
I saw two lion and three foxes.
I seen two lions and three foxes.
questions.rule: Two needs the plural lions, and the simple past of see is saw, not seen.

options: The foxes is clever.
The foxes are clever.
The fox are clever.
questions.rule: Fox → foxes, and a plural subject takes are.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: After the lion had ate his meal, he left the remains.
After the lion had eaten his meal, he left the remains.
After the lion has eaten his meal, he left the remains.
questions.rule: The earlier past action takes the past perfect: had + past participle = had eaten.

options: The camel carried a heavy luggage across the desert.
The camel carried heavy luggages across the desert.
The camel carried heavy luggage across the desert.
questions.rule: Luggage is uncountable: no a and no -s.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: fallen
falling
fall

questions.rule: The past perfect is had + past participle. The participle of fall is fallen.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
many
most

questions.rule: Of all compares more than two, so use the superlative: the most watchful.

options: best
good
better
questions.rule: The pattern the more ..., the + comparative needs a comparative: good → better.

options: slices
slice
breads
questions.rule: Bread is uncountable, so we count the unit: a few slices of bread.
Past perfect: had + past participle (had eaten) shows an action finished before a past time.

chat: Why didn't Neha come to the party last night?
options: She had already left for Pune with her parents.
She had already leave for Pune with her parents.
She had already leaving for Pune with her parents.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had left.

questions.source: The lion had seen a camel before.
options: The lion had not saw a camel before.
The lion did not had seen a camel before.
The lion had not seen a camel before.
questions.rule: Put not after had and keep the participle: had not seen.

options: This country are big.
This country is big.
This countries is big.
questions.rule: In the singular: these → this, countries → country, are → is.

options: How many milk and how much eggs do we need?
How much milk and how much eggs do we need?
How much milk and how many eggs do we need?
questions.rule: How much + uncountable (milk); how many + countable plural (eggs).

options: The vulture, whose wings were strong, flew ahead.
The vulture, who wings were strong, flew ahead.
The vulture, which wings were strong, flew ahead.
questions.rule: Whose shows possession: the wings belong to the vulture.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: have
had
having

questions.rule: The film started before we reached (past), so use the past perfect: had already started.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: informed
information
informing

questions.rule: Information is uncountable, so it never takes -s.

questions.after: master was a trader, followed the fox.
options: whose
who
which
questions.rule: Whose shows possession: the master belongs to the camel.

questions.before: Of all the courtiers, the fox was the
options: cleverer
cleverest
more clever
questions.rule: Of all compares more than two, so use the superlative: the cleverest.
Pattern: The more ..., the + comparative ... Both halves use a comparative.

chat: Good morning! What would you like?
options: Two packets of biscuits and a litre of milk, please.
Two packet of biscuits and a litre of milk, please.
Two packets of biscuits and a litre of milks, please.
questions.rule: Two packets is plural; milk is uncountable, so a litre of milk.

options: The one who my uncle gave me.
The one that my uncle gave me.
The one whose my uncle gave me.
questions.rule: For things, use that or which. Who is for people.

questions.source: The fox was clever. He thought of a plan.
options: The fox who was clever, he thought of a plan.
The fox, who was clever, thinks of a plan.
The fox, who was clever, thought of a plan.
questions.rule: Who replaces he, so don't repeat the subject. Keep the past tense: thought.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: There isn't much water in the pot, isn't it?
There aren't much water in the pot, are there?
There isn't much water in the pot, is there?
questions.rule: Water takes is. A negative there isn't takes a positive tag: is there?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: When we had reached the station, the train already left.
When we reached the station, the train had already left.
When we reached the station, the train has already left.
questions.rule: The train left first, so it takes the past perfect (had left); the later action is simple past (reached).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: are
be
was

questions.rule: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb: This news was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
were
be

questions.rule: Both the leopards is plural, so the past continuous is were resting.

options: some
many
a few
questions.rule: Money is uncountable, so use some; many and a few need countable nouns.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Comparative + than; a positive statement with was takes the tag wasn't he?
Who comes right after the person it describes: Komal, who lives ...

chat: Have you finished the project report?
options: Yes, I finished it yesterday.
Yes, I have finished it yesterday.
Yes, I had finish it yesterday.
questions.rule: With a finished past time like yesterday, use the simple past (finished), not the present perfect.

questions.source: The camel was the tallest animal in the group.
options: No other animal in the group was so tall than the camel.
No other animal in the group was as tall as the camel.
No other animal in the group was taller as the camel.
questions.rule: Superlative → positive: No other ... was as tall as ...

questions.source: The fox was the cleverest of all the courtiers.
options: The fox was cleverer than any other courtier.
The fox was cleverer than all other courtier.
The fox was more cleverer than any other courtier.
questions.rule: Superlative → comparative: cleverer than any other + singular noun. Never more cleverer.

options: The most water you drink in summer, the fresher you will feel.
The more waters you drink in summer, the fresher you will feel.
The more water you drink in summer, the fresher you will feel.
questions.rule: Pattern: the more ..., the + comparative. Water is uncountable, so no -s.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The courtiers realised that they had making a terrible mistake.
The courtiers realised that they had made a terrible mistake.
The courtiers realised that they had make a terrible mistake.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had made.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: whose
which
who

questions.rule: The relative pronoun is the subject of owned, so use who, not whom.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: many
little
less

questions.rule: A few is for countable nouns. With uncountable water, use a little.

questions.after: never met a lion before that day, so he was surprised.
options: has
have
had
questions.rule: An action before another past moment (before that day) takes the past perfect: had never met.
Who follows the people it describes (the doctors who ...); had saved is the earlier action.

chat: Why was Aarav so happy yesterday evening?
options: He had won the chess match that morning.
He had win the chess match that morning.
He has won the chess match that morning.
questions.rule: The win came before the evening (both past), so use had won. Has won can't go with that morning.

chat: Shall I pack some food for your school trip?
options: Yes, please. Just a little sandwiches and a few juice.
Yes, please. Just a few sandwich and a little juice.
Yes, please. Just a few sandwiches and a little juice.
questions.rule: A few + plural countable (sandwiches); a little + uncountable (juice).

questions.prompt: Change into a question without changing the meaning.
questions.source: The lion had never seen a camel.
options: Has the lion ever seen a camel?
Had the lion ever seen a camel?
Did the lion had ever seen a camel?
questions.rule: Move had before the subject and change never to ever: Had the lion ever seen ...?

questions.source: The vulture saw a desert. It was a few miles away.
options: The vulture saw a desert which was a few miles away.
The vulture saw a desert which it was a few miles away.
The vulture saw a desert who was a few miles away.
questions.rule: Which replaces it (a thing), so don't repeat it.
